indicator_rule: Indicators meet Gentry's test. Probabilities come directly from the 82-member multi-model ensemble (31 NOAA GEFS + 51 ECMWF IFS 0.25 deg) and map to ICD 203 likelihood terms via tic-doctrine. Transient hourly hazards require at least 3 hours in a UTC day (2 hours for freezing rain) so a brief shower does not colour a 24-hour operational window.
emerging_concerns: Additional operational stations (alternates in config/points.json) can be promoted to primary zone points if operations shift.

indicators.text: Operational weather hazard reaches Amber on the likelihood-by-impact matrix within 72 hours
indicators.rule: Ensemble probability >= 0.45 for a moderate-impact threshold or >= 0.20 for a severe-impact threshold on at least one UTC day in the next 72 hours

indicators.text: Operational weather hazard reaches Red on the likelihood-by-impact matrix within 72 hours
indicators.rule: Ensemble probability >= 0.45 for a severe-impact threshold on at least one UTC day in the next 72 hours

indicators.text: Extended low-light night window (>= 6 hours of nautical darkness with moon down or under 25% lit)
indicators.rule: dark_low_light_min >= 360 minutes between local solar noon and next solar noon

indicators.text: One of the two ensemble models is missing or failed to return members
indicators.rule: fewer than 2 independent ensemble models returned hourly members for the station

warning_problems.title: Operational weather degradation in a watched conflict zone
warning_problems.issue_on_change: Issue a warning item on the contract v2 feed when a zone's 72-hour stoplight reaches Amber or Red.
warning_problems.deactivation: Returns to routine when all 3 upcoming UTC days fall to Yellow or Green.

hypotheses.statement: Sustained weather conditions will degrade aviation, UAS/ISR, maritime or ground mobility in the zone
Weather remains within normal operating limits or passes in brief (< 3 h) local showers
Model outage or single-model bias (one ensemble system missing)
